item: glass-expansion: integrate Liquid Glass in more areas, starting with the queue screen (lyrics page and full-player top bar excluded)
currentBehaviour:
Overall: the outer surfaces of nearly every screen are already real Liquid Glass. A sweep of every `.fill(` / `.background(` in App/Features (Lyrics excluded) found 279 hits (re-counted). Almost all are deliberate fills sitting on a glass parent, which is what AGENTS.md:43-45 requires ("controls on a glass card are fills (PressScaleButtonStyle) or join via glassEffectUnion"). Examples: SettingsRows.swift:428 `SettingsFillButton` "plain fills (they sit on glass)", SpotifyComponents.swift:139 `SpotifyFilledButton`, and the icon chips and badges in rows and cards. Features use no toolbar content (only `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .navigationBar)`), no `pickerStyle(.segmented)`, no `.bordered` and no Material blur. The only system `Form`s are the developer screens (Developer/DiagnosticsView.swift:24, LibraryImportDebugView.swift:18). I compared main's CI shots (run 37142339689, artifact shots-c7dee2d…, in the scratchpad at shots/shots/*.png) against the code. Reviewer re-check: queue-light.png shows a flat white sheet, while sleepTimer-light.png shows the player through the sheet's glass. The queue reads as "not glass" for three concrete reasons:

1. **The sheet is opaque.** RouteDestinations.swift:50 presents `QueueSheet().pixlSheet(detents: [.large])` (`pixlSheet` = `presentationDetents` + drag indicator, SheetScaffold.swift:36-39). iOS 26 makes a sheet opaque at full height ("When a half sheet expands to full height, it transitions to a more opaque appearance", Adopting Liquid Glass). So the glass rows (QueueSheet.swift:567-568) sit on a flat white or black sheet and look like plain frosted cards. The sleep-timer sheet sizes its own height detent (SleepTimerSheet.swift:72, `fittedSheetDetent`) and shows the player through its glass.
2. **The toolbar buttons are solid fills.** QueueSheet.swift:207-245 draws a tinted glass capsule (227) holding three opaque circles: `toolbarButton` 247-260 uses `.background(Circle().fill(active ? theme.primary : theme.surfaceContainer))` at 254. Android draws backdrop-refracting `GlassIconButton`s (ui/glass/GlassComponents.kt:163) ON a `glassPanel` capsule (QueueBottomSheet.kt:1435-1531, panel at 1460-1466). That is glass on glass, which AGENTS.md:43-45 rules out on iOS, so the port made the circles fills. kt:983: the toolbar and FAB "refract the queue scrolling directly behind them". The iOS precedent for "liquidifying" such a row is PlayerToggleRow.swift:7-10/24-68: no capsule, each segment its own interactive glass in one container (Hoa, 2026-10-03).
3. **The ⋯ menu doesn't morph.** menuOverlay 264-300 is a scrim plus a gradient to surfaceContainerLowest (267-268, as Android kt:1038-1080). Three glass pills sit on top (`menuButton` 302-318, 18 pt radius, prominent tints) in a plain VStack(spacing: 10) at 272. There is no GlassEffectContainer; they slide in with `.move(edge: .bottom)` (292) under a root `.animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.2), value: isMenuExpanded)` (69). The ⋯ circle (228-241) only rotates. The modal semantics (`.isModal`, escape action, `queue.menu`) sit on the overlay (296-299), and the list is `.accessibilityHidden(isMenuExpanded)` (57). Context: on 2026-10-02 Hoa wanted the system "exploding" menu morph on small menus, "not on full-screen surfaces such as the queue", so "the queue keeps its own menu" (docs/design.md:693-709).

Smaller queue details:
- Swipe-to-remove reveal: an opaque `Capsule().fill(errorContainer)` at 508. Android draws this as a plain `Box.background` (kt:2033-2040), not a Material Surface. Making it glass would add a second glass layer to a lazy row, created mid-gesture (AGENTS.md:48: one glass layer per row). Leave it.
- The row ⋮ (556) is a fill on row glass, which is correct, so leave it.
- The header "Queue" capsule (122) and the undo bar (356) are already glass.
- The song sheet opened from the queue is `.large` too (73).

Queue siblings:
- **SleepTimerSheet.swift:** all six surfaces are glass (42, 115 ×2 via sliderGroup, 139, 158, 174), but none share a GlassEffectContainer. "Custom time" and "Cancel timer" are 6 pt apart at 147. The system Slider/Toggle inside become glass knobs while dragged.
- **SaveQueueAsPlaylistSheet.swift:**
  - The name field and search capsule (35-60, glass at 170 and 59) are 12 pt apart with no container. The field also carries a redundant `.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16))` at 43, the same shape as its glass.
  - The Save pill is a fill, `Capsule().fill(theme.primary)` at 224, on the glass bottom capsule at 233.
  - It has no screenshot test and no DemoScreen id. It is a fullScreenCover from QueueSheet.swift:78. No UI test uses `saveQueue.save`, `editSong.save`, `reorder.done`, `queue.timer`, `queue.more` or `queue.menu`.

Elsewhere, the standalone non-glass surfaces I found (most visible first):
- **Full player, outside the top bar:**
  - NowPlayingView.swift:298-306: the loading spinner sits in `Circle().fill(chip)` (304, chip = onPrimary @ 0.8 at 279), next to the glass lyrics and AI circles in `GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 6)` at 309. Android draws it as a Material `Surface(shape = CircleShape, color = chipColor)` (FullPlayerContent.kt:1630-1644), so it should be glass under decision 10.
  - PlayerSeekBar.swift:145-153: the file-info pill is `.background(color.opacity(0.14), in: Capsule())` (152), inside the 4 Hz TimelineView (32-38). Android: a Material `Surface` (FullPlayerContent.kt:2090-2096), so glass under decision 10.
- **DevicesSheet.swift:119-126:** the AirPlay and Bluetooth glass tiles are 12 pt apart without a container (perf rule only). Each tile carries an `AirPlayRoutePicker` (AVRoutePickerView) overlay as its tap target (225). No route picker sits inside a GlassEffectContainer anywhere yet.
- **GenreDetailView.swift:**
  - The artist group header (250-266) is a plain `.background(theme.surfaceContainerHigh)` (264) + clipShape (265-266). Android's `GenreArtistHeader` is a Material `Surface(surfaceContainerHigh)` inside a `Surface(surfaceContainerLow @ 0.5)` (GenreDetailScreen.kt:865-871), so this is a missed decision-10 conversion.
  - The album header (267-296) is a groupFill with a filled play circle (287). Android uses an `IconButton` with primary container colours (kt:983-990), which is a glass circle under decision 10.
  - The closest glass precedent is the artist page's `AlbumSectionHeader` (ArtistDetailView.swift:273-325, pixlGlass at 324, play circle a fill at 310).
- **StatsView.swift:134-188:** the collapsing header fades in a solid `surfaceContainerHigh` band (187), under the back/refresh GlassCircleButtons (166-173) and the range GlassPillRow (181-183). SettingsScaffold.swift:167-173 does the same job with a glass bar (`pixlGlass(in: Rectangle(), tint: surfaceContainerHigh @ GlassTint.bar)`), under one glass back circle (187-189).
- **PlaylistEditorView.swift:**
  - The top bar is a solid `surfaceContainer` (95). It sits in a VStack above the content (37-53), so nothing scrolls under it.
  - The "Auto-generated collage" placeholder (374) and the "Pick Image" button tile (430) are solid 32 pt tiles, on the flat `surface` page (54). Android draws them as plain `Box.background` (CreatePlaylistScreen.kt:1086-1090).
- **Floating action bars:** each is a glass panel with filled primary pills on it, by rule:
  - Edit song Cancel/Save: EditSongSheet.swift:309 and 331 on the bar at 338.
  - Library reorder Done: LibrarySheets.swift:320 on 327.
  - Genre Quick Fill Next: GenreSheets.swift:302 on 310.
  - Save as playlist Save: SaveQueueAsPlaylistSheet.swift:224 on 233.
  - AiPlaylistLabView.swift:134-174 is the existing pattern that already puts glass pills in a GlassEffectContainer over an opaque strip.
- **Other `.large`-only sheets render opaque the same way:**
  - songInfo (RouteDestinations.swift:51), aiPlaylist (57), taisChat (58).
  - SongOptionsSheet.swift:61, LibraryView.swift:473/476/497, PlaylistDetailView.swift:133/140, GenreDetailView.swift:216.
- **Lowest:** the developer `Form`s.

Not converted, by design: the content panels behind glass rows (LibraryView.swift:169, PlaylistDetailView.swift:285, grouped rows at ArtistDetailView.swift:255-258 and GenreDetailView.swift:315-326). Making those glass would put the glass rows on glass.

options.name: A: Queue first plus targeted fixes (recommended)
options.description: Queue: the toolbar circles become glass circles (dropping the backing capsule, as PlayerToggleRow did); with Hoa's OK the ⋯ circle morphs into the menu pills inside one GlassEffectContainer, otherwise the pills just get their own container. Group the sleep-timer and save-sheet surfaces into containers. Then the standalone fixes: the player spinner and file-info pill (both Material Surfaces on Android), the genre headers (Material Surface / IconButton on Android), the Stats header, the playlist-editor tiles. The sheet-detent change is behind an owner decision.
options.pros: Fixes exactly what Hoa sees on the queue. The toolbar change follows the toggle row Hoa already approved (PlayerToggleRow.swift:7-10). Several items are missed decision-10 conversions (spinner chip, file-info pill, genre artist header, genre play button), so they also improve parity. Uses only iOS 26.0 APIs and no Compat27. Small, reviewable diffs covered by existing screenshot classes.
options.cons: Android draws glass circles on a glass capsule; iOS can't stack glass (AGENTS.md:43-45), so the capsule goes and the row looks like the player's toggle row rather than Android's. Without the detent change the queue sheet stays opaque at full height, so the glass refracts only the rows scrolling under the toolbar.

options.name: B: A + translucent partial-height sheets
options.description: Also present the queue (and optionally song options, Daily Mix AI, Taizo) with a partial detent such as `.fraction(0.92)` instead of `[.large]`, so the system sheet stays Liquid Glass and the album-tinted full player shows through. presentationBackground is not overridden, so this stays within AGENTS.md.
options.pros: The biggest visible gain: the whole queue becomes glass over the player, as the sleep-timer and devices sheets already are.
options.cons: Breaks parity with Android's full-height opaque queue, so it needs Hoa's OK. Translucency lowers contrast over bright art. The player renders under the sheet (the animated ambient styles keep drawing at 30 Hz). Apple documents no threshold, so whether a 0.92 detent still gets the inset glass look must be proven on CI shots.

options.name: C: A/B + floating bars split into separate glass shapes
options.description: The Save/Done/Cancel/Next pills on glass bars (SaveQueue 224, EditSong 309/331, LibrarySheets 320, GenreSheets 302) become their own tinted glass capsules in a GlassEffectContainer. Two ways: drop the backing panel, or turn it into an opaque strip as AiPlaylistLabView.swift:134-174 does.
options.pros: Consistent everywhere: every primary action becomes interactive glass.
options.cons: Changes the Android 'floating toolbar' look on four screens, and the save sheet has no screenshot test yet.

options.name: D: System scroll-edge effect for top/bottom bars
options.description: Replace the solid collapsing headers (StatsView.swift:187, AiPlaylistLabView.swift:130/173) with `safeAreaBar` plus `scrollEdgeEffectStyle(_:for:)` instead of filled bands.
options.pros: The native iOS 26 idiom; no glass-on-glass under the bar's glass buttons (Apple: 'avoid … layering Liquid Glass elements on top of each other').
options.cons: Restructures layouts, the opposite of the port rule (Android bars are opaque; AiPlaylistLabView.swift:129 says so on purpose). Better done later, if at all.

recommendedPlan.change:
Toolbar circles (207-260). This step does not depend on the menu decision.
1. Remove the capsule glass at 227 (`.pixlGlass(in: Capsule(), tint: surfaceContainerHighest…)`). Keep `.padding(.horizontal, 12).padding(.vertical, 8).frame(maxHeight: .infinity)` so nothing moves.
2. In `toolbarButton`:
   - delete `.background(Circle().fill(...))` (254);
   - put `.contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))` on the Image;
   - replace `PressScaleButtonStyle()` (257) with `.buttonStyle(.plain)`, followed by `.pixlGlass(in: Circle(), tint: active ? theme.primary.opacity(GlassTint.prominent) : theme.surfaceContainer.opacity(GlassTint.surface), interactive: true)` and `.animation(.spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.75), value: active)`.
   This is the PlayerToggleRow.swift:49-68 recipe, but with `.regular` glass through pixlGlass, because the queue is not over media.
3. Container. If the ⋯ morph is NOT done, keep the existing `GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 2)` at 209: the gaps are 12 pt between circles and 12 + 4 = 16 pt to the ⋯ circle, so the shapes never blend at rest. If the morph IS done, the next entry replaces it with one body-level container.
4. Keep the labels "Toggle shuffle" / "Toggle repeat" / "Sleep timer", `accessibilityIdentifier("queue.timer")` and `.isSelected`. The ⋯ circle (228-241) stays as is: tertiaryContainer at prominent, interactive.

⋯ menu, only if Hoa picks the morph (body 40-71, toolbar 207-245, menuOverlay 264-300, menuButton 302-318):
1. Add `@Namespace private var glassNamespace`. Add `nonisolated private enum QueueGlassID: Hashable, Sendable { case menu, locate, clear }` inside QueueSheet. This is the house pattern (GlassPillRow.swift:46; docs/api-notes.md:190 explains why it must be nonisolated under MainActor default isolation). Never name anything `FAB…` or `Material…`: ci/check-forbidden.sh's material pattern fails the build.
2. The body's ZStack(alignment: .bottom) becomes, in order:
   - the list VStack, keeping `.accessibilityHidden(isMenuExpanded)` (57);
   - `if isMenuExpanded { menuScrim }`, which is the scrim + gradient from 266-271 with `.ignoresSafeArea()`, `.onTapGesture { closeMenu() }` and `.transition(.opacity.animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.2)))`;
   - ONE unconditional `GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 8) { ZStack(alignment: .bottom) { if isMenuExpanded { menuPills(canLocate:).padding(.bottom, 36) } else { toolbar.padding(.bottom, 16) } } }`;
   - the undo bar, unchanged and OUTSIDE the container. It overlaps the open menu, so inside the container it would blend.
3. `toolbar` loses its own container (209) and returns the HStack.
   - The ⋯ circle: `.pixlGlass(...)` followed by `.glassEffectID(QueueGlassID.menu, in: glassNamespace)`. The ID goes after the glass, as in Apple's examples.
   - Each of the three circles gets `.glassEffectTransition(.materialize)` after its pixlGlass. They then fade instead of being pulled into the Save pill, which overlaps the toolbar's area.
4. `menuPills` is the VStack(spacing: 10) from 272-290. Give `menuButton` an `id: QueueGlassID` parameter and apply `.glassEffectID(id, in: glassNamespace)` after its pixlGlass (316-317).
   - "Save as playlist", the bottom pill nearest the toolbar, uses `.menu`, so the ⋯ circle morphs into it and back.
   - Locate and Clear use `.locate` / `.clear` plus `.glassEffectTransition(.materialize)`.
   - The modal semantics go on the pills VStack itself, which exists only while open: `.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)`, `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isModal)`, `.accessibilityAction(.escape) { closeMenu() }`, `.accessibilityIdentifier("queue.menu")`.
   - Do NOT put these on a wrapper around the container. That wrapper also holds the toolbar while the menu is closed, so `.isModal` would trap VoiceOver in the toolbar, and the escape action would swallow the gesture that dismisses the sheet.
   - Do NOT apply them with an `if` around the container either. That changes the container's identity and kills the morph.
   - The identifier may be dropped inside the container (docs/performance.md:104-106). No test uses it.
5. Animation:
   - `closeMenu()` is `withAnimation(PixlMotion.selection) { isMenuExpanded = false }`.
   - The ⋯ action is `withAnimation(PixlMotion.selection) { isMenuExpanded.toggle() }`.
   - Each menu action calls closeMenu(), then sets its flag as today (276-288).
   - Delete `.animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.2), value: isMenuExpanded)` at 69. An implicit animation on the root would override the withAnimation spring for the whole subtree.
   - Drop `.transition(.move(edge: .bottom)...)` at 292.
   - Keep `.pixlHaptic(.selection, trigger: isMenuExpanded)` (71).
6. The ⋯ Button keeps the label "More actions". PlayerScreenshotTests.swift:48-49 taps it by identifier OR label, and `queue.more` can be lost inside a container.

Fallback (no morph, or the shared-id morph looks wrong on the phone): keep today's structure, with the toolbar in its own container under the scrim and menuOverlay as is. Wrap only the three pills in their own `GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 8)` inside menuOverlay (perf rule; 10 pt gaps), and keep the `.move` transition. Never put the pills and a visible toolbar in one container: the Save pill (bottom 36-84 pt) overlaps the toolbar (bottom 16-86 pt), and they would blend.

Only if Hoa says yes (option B): line 50, `QueueSheet().pixlSheet(detents: [.large])` becomes `.pixlSheet(detents: [.fraction(0.92)])`, a single partial detent, so the system keeps the Liquid Glass sheet. Never touch presentationBackground.
- Optionally do the same at QueueSheet.swift:73 (the song sheet opened from the queue) and line 51 (songInfo).
- In the shots, check that the sheet really renders inset and translucent at 0.92. Apple documents no threshold; if it doesn't, try 0.85.
- Check that the 120 pt list bottom padding (QueueSheet.swift:167), the undo bar (`.padding(.bottom, 96)`, line 65) and the toolbar still clear the home indicator.

Wrap the content VStack (36-67) in `GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 4)` inside the ScrollView. Keep `.padding`/`.measuringHeight` on the VStack inside the container, so the fitted detent measures the same thing. Its gaps are 6-24 pt, so nothing blends at rest. The six glass shapes then render together, including the 6 pt-apart Custom time / Cancel timer pair at 147. No visual change intended. Low priority: whether an interactive press's swell stays inside a 6 pt gap is the same open question as pending on-device check 2 (docs/performance.md:146).

1. Wrap the name field and search capsule (VStack 35-60) in `GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 6)`. Delete the redundant `.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16, style: .continuous))` at 43. It repeats the glass shape at 170, and a clip on a container child is an untested interaction.
2. Only if Hoa picks option C, the bottom bar (201-234): turn the Save pill fill (224) into its own `pixlGlass(in: Capsule(), tint: theme.primary.opacity(GlassTint.prominent), interactive: !selected.isEmpty)`. Then make the summary its own glass capsule (`secondaryContainer` at prominent) beside it, in one container, instead of the Save fill sitting on the bar's glass at 233.
3. Keep the `saveQueue.save` identifier. Nothing looks it up today.

Loading spinner (298-306).
1. Replace `.background(Circle().fill(chip))` (304) with `.glassEffect(Glass.clear.tint(theme.onPrimary.opacity(GlassTint.playerChrome)), in: Circle())`: clear glass over media, NOT `playerGlass` (358-360), because that one is interactive and this is not a button. Remove `let chip` (279) once unused.
2. Move the `if playback.isPreparing { … }` block, with its `.padding(.trailing, 8)` and transition, to be the FIRST child of the `HStack(spacing: 12)` at 310 inside the container at 309. The gaps don't change: title to spinner stays 12 pt (outer HStack spacing at 280), and spinner to lyrics circle stays 8 + 12 = 20 pt, well above the container's 6.
3. Keep `.animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.3), value: playback.isPreparing)` at 321.
This is decision-10 parity: Android draws a Material circle Surface (FullPlayerContent.kt:1630-1644). The chip goes from onPrimary @ 0.8 to clear @ 0.14, like its neighbours (GlassStyle.swift:16-18). Check the spinner's contrast in the expanded shots.

File-info pill (145-153): replace `.background(color.opacity(0.14), in: Capsule())` (152) with `.glassEffect(Glass.clear.tint(color.opacity(0.14)), in: Capsule())`, non-interactive. This is decision-10 parity: Android uses a Material Surface (FullPlayerContent.kt:2090-2096). The pill lives inside the 4 Hz TimelineView closure (32-38). The modifier is re-applied with identical values each tick, which is acceptable. If a hitch shows, hoist the pill out of the closure, since it doesn't depend on position.

Optional, perf/rule only, no visual change: wrap the AirPlay/Bluetooth tile HStack(spacing: 12) at 119-126 in `GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 6)`. Each tile's tap target is an `AirPlayRoutePicker` UIKit overlay (225). No route picker sits inside a container yet, so on CI (testDevices*) and on the phone, check that tapping a tile still opens the system route picker. Leave the icon-chip fills (145, 208, 341) and DeviceBadge (373) alone: they sit on glass.

1. Artist header (250-266): replace `.background(theme.surfaceContainerHigh)` plus the clipShape (264-266) with `.pixlGlass(in: UnevenRoundedRectangle(topLeadingRadius: 24, bottomLeadingRadius: 0, bottomTrailingRadius: 0, topTrailingRadius: 24, style: .continuous), tint: theme.surfaceContainerHigh.opacity(GlassTint.surface))`. This is decision-10 parity (Android Material Surface, GenreDetailScreen.kt:865-871), matching ArtistDetailView.swift:324. The icon chip (256) stays a fill.
2. The album header (267-296) stays groupFill, because it continues the grouped surface. Its play Button (280-290, fill at 287) becomes `GlassCircleButton(systemImage: "play.fill", accessibilityLabel: "Play album", size: 40, iconSize: 16, tint: theme.primary.opacity(GlassTint.prominent), foreground: theme.onPrimary) { if let first = albumSongs.first { playback.play(first, in: playOrder) } }`. The memberwise init takes a trailing `action` (GlassButtons.swift:44-53). This is Android's IconButton (kt:983-990): glass on a fill, so it is allowed. The icon weight becomes .medium instead of .semibold.

Only if Hoa says yes to the glass top bar. StatsHeader (134-188): replace `.background(theme.surfaceContainerHigh.opacity(solidAlpha))` (187) with SettingsScaffold's glass bar recipe (SettingsScaffold.swift:167-173): `.background { Rectangle().fill(.clear).pixlGlass(in: Rectangle(), tint: theme.surfaceContainerHigh.opacity(GlassTint.bar)).opacity(solidAlpha).ignoresSafeArea(edges: .top).allowsHitTesting(false) }`. Unlike Settings (one circle on its bar), this bar also carries the range GlassPillRow and two circles. That is the layering Apple advises against, accepted here only by the Settings precedent: check the stats-scrolled shots.

1. Collage placeholder at 374: replace the fill with `.pixlGlass(in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 32, style: .continuous), tint: theme.surfaceContainerHighest.opacity(GlassTint.surface))`. `GlassCard` would tint at GlassTint.container (0.62) instead (GlassCard.swift:22-23), so pick one deliberately.
2. The "Pick Image" tile at 430: drop the fill inside the label and apply the same pixlGlass with `interactive: true` after `.buttonStyle(.plain)` (433).
3. Leave the top bar at 95 solid. It sits in a VStack above the content (37-53) with nothing scrolling under it, so glass would only render as a flat band over `surface`.

Only with option C: the floating-bar pills become glass, following AiPlaylistLabView.swift:134-174:
- EditSongSheet: Cancel/Save at 309/331 on the bar at 338.
- LibrarySheets: reorder Done at 320 on 327.
- GenreSheets: Quick Fill Next at 302 on 310.
Each pill becomes a `GlassPillButton` or a `pixlGlass(in: Capsule(), tint: role.opacity(GlassTint.prominent), interactive: true)` inside a `GlassEffectContainer`. The backing panel's glass becomes an opaque strip or goes away, to avoid glass-on-glass. Identifiers `editSong.save` / `reorder.done` may be dropped inside the container. No test uses them.

1. PlayerScreenshotTests: add `testQueueMenuDark` (`capture("queue", "dark", ready: "screen.queue", tap: "More actions", name: "queueMenu")`).
2. Add `testSaveQueueLight`:
   - launch `queue`, tap "More actions" by identifier-or-label, then tap the "Save as playlist" button by label;
   - wait for `sheet.saveQueue`, then snapshot `saveQueue-light`.
   The `capture` helper (83-96) takes one tap, so write it like the drag tests. The name field autofocuses after 250 ms (SaveQueueAsPlaylistSheet.swift:96-99), so the shot may include the keyboard.
3. GlassAccessibilityTests: add `testQueueControlsKeepButtonTraits`. Launch `queue` (dark) and assert that `app.buttons` contains labels "Toggle shuffle" and "More actions". Tap "More actions" and assert "Clear queue" is a button. This covers the new containers per docs/performance.md:139-141.

1. api-notes.md: add `View.glassEffectTransition(_:)` + `GlassEffectTransition.matchedGeometry` / `.materialize` (iOS 26.0). glassEffectID is already at line 190. If used, also add `PresentationDetent.fraction(_:)` (iOS 16) and `glassEffectUnion(id:namespace:)` / `scrollEdgeEffectStyle(_:for:)` (iOS 26.0).
2. design.md: add a dated 'Glass expansion (owner change 2026-10-07)' note. Cover the queue toolbar circles as separate glass (PlayerToggleRow precedent, because Android's glass-on-glass capsule can't be ported), the ⋯ decision, and the detent decision. If the morph lands, update 'The queue keeps its own menu' at design.md:709.
3. performance.md: note the queue's menu/toolbar container, and that its modal accessibility sits on the pills inside it.
4. parity.md: note the decision-10 fixes (genre artist header and play circle, player spinner chip and file-info pill).
5. Add a dated handoff note.
6. Commit with `[shots:PlayerScreenshotTests,LibraryScreenshotTests,HomeStatsScreenshotTests,GlassAccessibilityTests,ScreenshotTests/testNowPlayingDark,SpotifyConnectScreenshotTests/testNowPlayingChipLight]`. For the morph, consider a `[record:...]` filming class like MenuRecordingTests (design.md:710).

risks: Nothing compiles locally: every visual judgement (toolbar circles without the backing capsule, the morph, glass headers) rests on CI screenshots. The ⋯ morph is only really visible on the phone or in a `[record:]` filming run.

Shared-id morph is an extrapolation. Apple's article says to give each effect a unique identifier and lets container spacing plus geometry decide which shapes morph. Giving the removed ⋯ circle and the inserted Save pill the same glassEffectID mirrors matchedGeometryEffect and the codebase's moving selection id (GlassPillRow.swift:121, api-notes.md:190), but Apple never shows it for a removed and an inserted view. Keep the fallback ready.

The root `.animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.2), value: isMenuExpanded)` at QueueSheet.swift:69 must go. An implicit animation on an ancestor overrides the withAnimation spring for the subtree and would flatten the morph.

Conditional modifiers kill the morph: an `if isMenuExpanded { container.modifier(...) } else { container }` changes the container's structural identity. Keep the container unconditional and switch only its content.

Accessibility inside GlassEffectContainer: children can lose their accessibility identifiers but keep labels and traits (docs/performance.md:104-106, GlassAccessibilityTests.swift:3-6).
- `.isModal` and the escape action on the pills VStack inside the container are unverified on device. The list is already accessibilityHidden while the menu is open (QueueSheet.swift:57), so the modal trap isn't load-bearing.
- A wrapper outside the container would make the closed toolbar modal and swallow the sheet-dismiss escape.
- Add a VoiceOver check to the on-device list.
glassEffectUnion merges only effects with the same shape and glass variant (Apple docs), so it can't group active and inactive tinted circles. Don't use it for the toolbar.

Overlap blending: the Save pill overlaps the toolbar area and the undo bar overlaps the open menu. Never keep overlapping glass in one container on screen at the same time: the toolbar leaves while the menu is open, and the undo bar stays outside the container.

Glass-on-glass:
- The recommended toolbar change removes the capsule glass rather than stacking.
- The Stats glass bar puts a pill row and two circles over glass. That is accepted only by the Settings precedent, and Apple advises against layering glass.
- Swipe reveal: left as a fill on purpose. A glass reveal would be a second glass layer per lazy row, created mid-gesture (AGENTS.md:48, perf rule 8).

research:
Apple, Adopting Liquid Glass (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technologyoverviews/adopting-liquid-glass), re-fetched as docs JSON:
- "half sheets are inset from the edge of the display to allow content to peek through from beneath them. When a half sheet expands to full height, it transitions to a more opaque appearance to help maintain focus on the task". This explains why the `[.large]` queue looks solid.
- "If you apply these effects to custom elements, make sure to combine them using a GlassEffectContainer".
- "avoid overcrowding or layering Liquid Glass elements on top of each other". This matters for the Stats glass bar under glass pills.
- "For controls like sliders and toggles, the knob transforms into Liquid Glass during interaction".

Apple, Applying Liquid Glass to custom views (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/applying-liquid-glass-to-custom-views), re-fetched:
- A container spacing larger than the layout gap makes shapes blend at rest.
- glassEffectUnion "combines all effects with a similar shape, Liquid Glass effect, and ID into a single shape".
- "For effects you want to add or remove that are positioned within the container's assigned spacing, the default transition type is matchedGeometry"; use materialize for effects farther apart than the spacing.
- "Associate each Liquid Glass effect with a unique identifier within a namespace … SwiftUI uses the spacing provided to the effect container along with the geometry of the shapes themselves to determine when and which appropriate shapes to morph into and out of."
- The plan's shared id between the removed ⋯ circle and the inserted Save pill is therefore an extrapolation, not the documented pattern. Confidence on that step is lower.

Signatures, checked against the developer.apple.com JSON:
- `@MainActor @preconcurrency func glassEffectTransition(_ transition: GlassEffectTransition) -> some View`, iOS 26.0 (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/glasseffecttransition(_:)).
- `GlassEffectTransition`: `static var matchedGeometry` / `static var materialize` / `identity`, iOS 26.0 (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/glasseffecttransition). materialize "will fade in content and animate in or out the glass material but will not attempt to match the geometry of any other glass effects".
- `nonisolated func glassEffectID(_ id: (some Hashable & Sendable)?, in namespace: Namespace.ID) -> some View`, iOS 26.0 (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/glasseffectid(_:in:)). Already in api-notes.md:190.
- `@MainActor @preconcurrency func glassEffectUnion(id: (some Hashable & Sendable)?, namespace: Namespace.ID) -> some View`, iOS 26.0 (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/glasseffectunion(id:namespace:)).
- `static func fraction(_ fraction: CGFloat) -> PresentationDetent`, iOS 16.0 (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/presentationdetent/fraction(_:)).
- `nonisolated func scrollEdgeEffectStyle(_ style: ScrollEdgeEffectStyle?, for edges: Edge.Set) -> some View`, iOS 26.0 (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/scrolledgeeffectstyle(_:for:)).

Third-party confirmation (https://nilcoalescing.com/blog/PresentingLiquidGlassSheetsInSwiftUI, 18 July 2025, re-fetched): sheets need "at least one partial height option, such as medium or a custom height detent" to get the Liquid Glass background; "When the sheet is expanded to the large detent, its background transitions to an opaque appearance". Neither source gives a threshold for a near-full fraction detent.
